narrative: OMX30 opens with modest tailwinds from overnight global resilience, but technical conviction remains fragile. The index sits 5.8% above its 200-day moving average in confirmed bull mode, yet RSI at 47.68 and weak ADX (3.4) signal directionless price action. US 10Y yields surging 43bp to 5.184% create a mixed backdrop: banks benefit from widening NIM expectations, but tech and real estate face DCF headwinds. Oil's sharp 3.63% drop relieves input-cost anxiety for industrials, while the VIX spike to 16.26 hints at underlying risk-off sentiment. With ADX below 18, all sector calls are reduced in confidence; traders should expect range-bound consolidation rather than directional commitment.
morningBrief: OMX30 bull market intact above 200-MA, but weak ADX (3.4) and neutral RSI (47.68) suggest consolidation bias rather than breakout. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) are the primary beneficiaries of surging US yields (+43bp), which should widen NIM outlook; watch for SEB resistance at recent highs. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo, Sandvik) get relief from oil's -3.63% crash, reducing cost inflation fears. Tech (Ericsson B, Hexagon B) faces headwinds from both yield compression in DCF models and NASDAQ's flat overnight performance—stay defensive here. Mining play Boliden remains neutral despite commodity weakness (gold -3.24%, copper -0.98%). Key support at 3085 (lower Bollinger band); resistance at 3180 (50-MA). Watch US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET for any shock that could reignite volatility. Position sizing tight given VIX spike and weak momentum indicators.
